report.summary: The cluster is healthy at the workload level (all astronomy-shop pods Running/ready, 0 restarts, no OOM/Eviction/Failed pods), but the application is failing on a PostgreSQL authentication mismatch for database user "otelu". The PostgreSQL 17.6 pod completed a fresh init run at 08:53:15-16 and from 08:54:06.152 onward logs `FATAL: password authentication failed for user "otelu"` (pg_hba.conf line 128, scram-sha-256) every few hundred milliseconds. All three services that use that database fail with their own errors: product-catalog (`failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"`, and `Product Not Found` for IDs that init.sql inserts), product-reviews (`psycopg2.OperationalError ... password authentication failed for user "otelu"`), and accounting (`Npgsql.PostgresException 28P01: password authentication failed for user "otelu"`). That propagates to recommendation, checkout, the llm product-assistant, frontend, frontend-proxy and the load-generator, which all return/record HTTP 500 or gRPC INTERNAL/NOT_FOUND errors. Exactly the three postgres-using Deployments were rolled out configuration-only right before the failures began (product-catalog 4 ReplicaSets, accounting 2, product-reviews 2, all other Deployments 1), and their DB connection strings changed from a 5-character to a 14-character password while the database was already initialized. The postgresql-init ConfigMap, the only readable definition of that credential, now declares `CREATE USER otelu WITH PASSWORD 'otelp_7k9m2q4x'` (14 characters). I therefore read this as a database password change applied to the clients/init.sql at ~08:53:58-08:54:09 that was never applied to the running database role (no ALTER ROLE / re-init), i.e. a credential mismatch whose origin is the changed DB credential configuration; the client-side credential values are redacted and the Secret product-catalog-db-conn is unreadable, and change history is not integrated, so I cannot prove which side of the mismatch changed last. Conclusion is partial for that reason.

Consistent with: init completed 08:53:15-16; the first FATAL appears at 08:54:06 after the replacement pods started; the superseded revisions carried a 5-character password and the live ones a 14-character password; postgresql's pod and Deployment were never rolled (single ReplicaSet, 0 restarts).

Alternative hypothesis that the evidence cannot exclude: the live role does hold the 14-character password now recorded in postgresql-init's init.sql ('otelp_7k9m2q4x') and the client-side credentials injected into the three Deployments / Secret product-catalog-db-conn are a different 14-character value; in that case the fault originates on the client credential side rather than in the ConfigMap. It cannot be decided because the client credential values are redacted in the deployment env output and Secret product-catalog-db-conn cannot be read at all.

recommendation.text: Recover by making the live database role and the application credential agree again: either ALTER ROLE otelu with the password now configured for the clients, or roll the client workloads (Secret product-catalog-db-conn and the accounting/product-reviews DB_CONNECTION_STRING values) back to the password the running role holds, then re-check that postgresql stops logging 28P01/`password authentication failed for user "otelu"` and that product-catalog ListProducts, product-reviews GetProductReviews and accounting order consumption succeed.

Treat the postgresql-init init.sql credential as a one-shot bootstrap secret only: any password change must also be applied to the running role (ALTER ROLE) or accompanied by a deliberate re-initialisation, otherwise a configuration-only rollout of the consuming Deployments breaks authentication exactly as observed here.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected as the cause: pod-level damage or resource problems (no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Failed event, every container ready with 0 restarts, the few Unhealthy events are startup probes of grafana, opensearch-0 and otel-collector-agent, and the FailedMount events are configmap-volume sync timeouts during that same startup).

Rejected as the cause: a flagd-injected fault. All feature flags are defaultVariant "off", and the errors are database authentication failures in the services' own logs, which no flag in this config injects.

Considered and set aside: Kafka. accounting logged `Confluent.Kafka.ConsumeException: Subscribed topic not available: orders: Broker: Unknown topic or partition` at 08:53:40, before the new pods came up, and the cart path (valkey) is healthy; nothing shows a Kafka failure accompanying the 08:54:06+ errors.
